gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Huawei Watch D2's cuff is an inflating airbag that only works when the watch is held level with the heart on a wrist 130–210 mm around, using whichever of the two included straps fits (M 130–160 mm, L 161–210 mm), and that Huawei itself warns that arrhythmia, a heart rate below 40 or above 180 bpm, or severe arteriosclerosis can make readings fail or come out wrong.
standout_why: I compared against the rival pages I could open: the FDA safety communication (cited), the Samsung press release (Samsung Mobile Press copy of the cited news.samsung.com post) and Hilo's blog (cited). The FDA page only says to check for authorization (product code DXN) and does not explain how any device measures. Samsung's page covers the cuffless method, the 28-day calibration and the Galaxy-phone requirement, and ChatGPT's answer already passed all of that on. Hilo's blog says only in general terms that wrist monitors must be kept at heart level, and it does not mention Huawei. None of these gives the D2's airbag wrist ranges, the posture rule in the maker's words, or the maker's list of conditions under which the cuff fails (arrhythmia, heart rate outside 40–180 bpm, arteriosclerosis). I could not read the cited Wareable D3 review (HTTP 403), the cited cardilog.app page (certificate error) or the TechRadar page (truncated), so one of them may partly cover this. That is why the score is 2 and not 3.
decides: This confirms that the cuff watch is the only kind in ChatGPT's picks that actually measures blood pressure rather than estimating it. It also adds conditions that ChatGPT left out. A shopper whose wrist is outside 130–210 mm, or who has atrial fibrillation or frequent premature beats, should not count on the D2's cuff and should use an upper-arm cuff instead. Turning on the D2's 24-hour monitoring cuts battery life to about 1 day. On the Samsung side, the feature needs a Galaxy phone on Android 12 or later and a separately bought upper-arm cuff every 28 days. Samsung also says its Health Monitor app works only on devices bought in a country where the service is offered.

findings.label: Wrist circumference range for the airbag cuff (two straps in box)
findings.value: M-sized strap 130–160 mm; L-sized strap 161–210 mm; overall 130–210 mm; strap width 26.5 mm
findings.note: Read from the UK spec page. The box contains the watch fitted with the L-sized airbag strap and a short strap, plus a spare M-sized airbag strap. This is the maker's UK page; there is no Huawei US product page.

findings.label: Posture the cuff measurement requires
findings.value: Watch level with the heart; elbow bent at 90° with the palm on the chest; seated and rested for at least 5 minutes; no talking or moving
findings.source_title: Blood pressure measurements on my HUAWEI WATCH D/D2 fail or generate no results
findings.note: Huawei quote: 'make sure that the device is level with your heart'. Fit rules: wear the watch about 3 cm (two fingers' width) from the palm, not over the wrist bone, with room for one finger under the strap.

findings.label: Conditions under which the maker says BP readings fail or are inaccurate
findings.value: Arrhythmia; heart rate below 40 or above 180 bpm; severe arteriosclerosis; frequent premature beats; severe anemia (weak pulse); cold wrist; pressure outside the pump's 0–300 mmHg range
findings.source_title: Blood pressure measurements on my HUAWEI WATCH D/D2 fail or generate no results
findings.note: Maker's own wording: 'Arrhythmia could cause measurement failure or inaccurate results'. This is a limit of oscillometric cuff measurement, which reads blood pressure from pulse oscillations under the inflating airbag.

findings.label: Battery life with 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM) on
findings.value: Up to 1 day (vs up to 6 days typical without ABPM)
findings.note: Huawei's test conditions: ABPM at 15-minute intervals, plus six manual BP and five ECG measurements per day.

findings.label: ABPM behaviour at night
findings.value: Default every 30 minutes by day and by night; at night the watch inflates and measures automatically without a reminder
findings.source_title: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) on your HUAWEI WATCH D2
findings.note: Huawei: 'Using ABPM will affect the Sleep breathing awareness feature and heart rate monitoring during sleep.' Huawei describes the readings as 'a reference for BP measurements'.

findings.label: Phone compatibility
findings.value: Android 8.0 or later; iOS 13.0 or later
findings.note: Unlike Samsung's feature, this works with an iPhone.

findings.label: BP feature requirements and method
findings.value: Estimates BP from a calibrated value using the watch's heart-rate sensor; needs recalibration with an upper-arm cuff (sold separately) every 28 days; requires a Samsung Galaxy phone on Android 12+ and a watch on Wear OS 4.0+ (Galaxy Watch4 and later, not Galaxy Fit)
findings.source_title: Samsung's Blood Pressure Monitoring Feature Now Available to U.S. Users in Samsung Health | Samsung Mobile Press
findings.note: Samsung also says the Health Monitor app works only on devices bought in a country where the service is offered, and that resetting the phone or reinstalling the app while abroad may restrict or disable it. The page does not say the BP feature is FDA-authorized.

findings.label: Method and regulatory scope
findings.value: Optical estimation at the wrist, recalibrated every 30 days by an included upper-arm cuff; only the cuff is FDA-cleared, not the band or the system; up to 35 readings a day
findings.source_title: Blood pressure wearables: Hilo Core vs. HLTH vs. Hume | Hilo Core
findings.note: Hilo: 'The clearance attaches to the cuff only.' The band withholds readings when it detects 'non-optimal conditions'.

findings.label: Market status and validation
findings.value: Discontinued by the manufacturer but may be available through certain outlets; passed clinical validation in a general population to a recognised protocol (Medaval ★★)
findings.source_title: Omron Heartguide BP8000 M HEM 6410T ZM | Medaval
findings.note: Medaval gives no date for the discontinuation. This contradicts ChatGPT's suggestion to 'verify current stock' of a current product. Omron's own US page was not checked.

findings.label: How to check FDA authorization of a BP wearable
findings.value: Search the FDA 510(k) database by device name; authorized BP devices generally carry product code DXN
findings.source_title: Do Not Use Unauthorized Devices for Measuring Blood Pressure: FDA Safety Communication
findings.note: Issued September 16, 2025. It covers 'unauthorized software features on wearables, such as smartwatches and smart rings, regardless of brand.' ChatGPT already cited this page.
